follow-up time: > 1 year after delivery (for one patient with incontinence)
cohort: 31,707 women with singleton pregnancies (179 with IBD and 31,528 without IBD) in a single centre between 2014 and 2018
finding: Although women with IBD had a higher rate of caesarean section, perineal trauma, including tears involving the anal sphincter, was equally uncommon in IBD and non-IBD patients.
mod_finding: This study found that women with IBD had a higher rate of cesarean section than non-IBD patients, but perineal trauma was equally uncommon in both groups.
